y-m-56-08.title: Which class use class library more?

y-m-56-08.material: Last month, 12 students for Class A and 9 for Class B use school class library. We never know total students for each class. Here 'class wey use am more' mean class where ratio of library users to all students in class higher. Remember each class fit get different student count.

y-m-56-08.s.s1.o.b: Class B (because class with few users probably get few students total too)

y-m-56-08.s.s1.explain: Ratio na number of students wey use library divided by all students in class. If totals unknown, you no fit tell whether 12 users be higher ratio. For example, if Class A get 60 students, 12/60=0.2; if Class B get 20, 9/20=0.45, so Class B higher. If Class A get 15 and Class B get 30, Class A higher.

y-m-56-02.material: Graph of function y = |x| get 'V' shape with vertex at (0, 0), where y=1 both when x=1 and when x=−1. (|x| read as 'the absolute value of x'.) Minjae write solution to find equation of graph after shifting this graph 2 units right (positive x-axis direction).

y-m-56-01.title: We fit call this correspondence a function?
y-m-56-01.topic: Meaning of function: correspondence where every input give exactly one result
y-m-56-01.goal: Test each correspondence with condition say every input get exactly one result; sort out which ones be functions, fix one correspondence wey no be function to make am one, and build function wey follow range condition.
y-m-56-01.material:
For class of 28 students, each student get one attendance number from 1 to 28, and each student get exactly one birthday (ignore leap years). Correspondence where every input give exactly one result na 'function'. Here result mean one number (or one attendance number); different results no count as one bundle. Four correspondences dey below.
(가) attendance number → month wey student born (January to December)
(나) birth month (January to December) → attendance numbers of students born that month
(다) natural number → number of divisors of that number
(라) natural number → numbers wey divide that number
y-m-56-01.thinking.0: Apply definition condition (one result for every input) to examples and decide
y-m-56-01.thinking.1: Explain with exact numbers why correspondence no be function
y-m-56-01.thinking.2: Build different functions wey follow range condition
y-m-56-01.prereq.0: Middle-school idea of function (relation where each x value give exactly one y value)
y-m-56-01.prereq.2: This task only show difficulty and support level H1 of generated batch; e no mean say subject dey assigned to one particular grade. Assumption: basic middle-school functions, geometry, and data already learned.
y-m-56-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose every correspondence wey fit count as function.

y-m-56-01.s.s1.r.a: This judgment say every input (attendance number) give exactly one birth month. You check definition condition.
y-m-56-01.s.s1.r.b: If you decide say 'students dey, so number don determine', check whether one month get many students born inside or no student at all.
y-m-56-01.s.s1.r.c: This judgment say number of divisors for each natural number na one single number.
y-m-56-01.s.s1.o.d: (라) natural number → numbers wey divide am
y-m-56-01.s.s1.r.d: One number fit get several divisors. Use number like 6 check whether 'one result for each input' hold.
y-m-56-01.s.s1.explain: For (가), each student get one birthday, so birth month determine as one month. For (다), each number get exactly one divisor-count. For (나), 28 students dey across 12 months, so at least one month gats get two or more students, and number no determine as one (some month fit also get no student). For (라), some numbers like 6 get several divisors, so result no be one fixed thing.
y-m-56-01.s.s2.prompt: All numbers wey function values fit take na 'range'. For function f with domain {1, 2, 3}, choose values f(1), f(2), f(3) and make three different functions whose range exactly {4, 5}. (Dem read f(1) as 'f of 1', f(2) as 'f of 2', and f(3) as 'f of 3'.)

y-m-56-01.s.s2.ok.c2: Both 4 and 5 show up as values.
